entry_points.text: Group alloc builds descriptor, id, stats, per-node records, writeback, reclaim work, pressure, peaks, socket stamp, legacy, kernel id, foreign table and gen state with unwind on failure. Early setup validates overflow, registers CPU handling and creates workqueues and caches; boot strings parse opt-outs and a deprecated swap switch.

Writeback startup clears state, inits spin lock, arms a deferrable timer, stamps dirty limit and inits completion accounting, returning status; shutdown cancels the timer synchronously and tears down completions with group wrappers delegating init, exit and size change. Flush merges interrupt-unsafe accounting then folds counters and clears markers. Attach optionally migrates the leader address space with task locking and marks tasks for lazy refresh; one build empties the reclaim step.

Status exposes byte usage, hierarchical and local events, formatted stats, per-node breakdowns after flushing, integer OOM mode accepting only zero or one, and manual reclaim. Proactive reclaim takes an amount with optional swappiness, needs exactly one of group or node target, and runs group or guarded node reclaim with minimum batch.

exports.text: Kernel charging uses current group, skips absent/root, tags head and refs on success. Splits propagate tags and add refs; uncharged heads exit early.

Folio charging resolves an owner then sizes a charge before commit, via address space, swap entry or current context. Swap charging pins by id, validates cache and reserves for non-root; uncharge reverses it.
Sockets bind to current group at alloc, release on free and move on inherit when owners differ. Alloc is skipped outside task context, when disabled, for root or inactive legacy.

Reclaim guards pair around direct reclaim with filesystem flag; low-level acquire and release take and drop the global map by caller address. Acquire briefly touches the MMU range map as an immediate pair. A barrier waits for queued per-group background work.
Swap files report current bytes, high and max with textual maximum, resettable peak and events. High uses a setter, max uses atomic exchange; all hide on root.
Helpers free by virtual versus slab address, resolve groups by numeric id, store min and low with upward recompute, and clear swap-backed counters.

hazards.text: Charge stability needs a stabilizer; foreign stamps and completions can race; ids must not publish before online; per-node shrinker and group pointers need mutex or RCU; poisoned unevictable and gen heads trap reuse, with exit warning on linked or populated state and freeing bloom storage. List, spin, RCU, atomic, cgroup and time helpers live elsewhere.

invariants.text: Folios link only when uncharged under page lock, LRU isolation or exclusive ownership; the accounting word holds the group, kernel-tagged for kernel charges. Root commits free; failures drop the temp ref.

Same-node migration reuses the source ref; cross-node resolves the same group at the destination. Replace and migrate need locked same-type same-size ends off reclaim lists; bad ends exit unchanged and collapse to root settles counters.

Foreign tracking reuses matching device and group slots or replaces the oldest idle slot with lazy timestamp refresh under a short cap. Flush clears recent idle stamps and triggers writeback by stored identities.
Alternate group writeback hooks are inert: init succeeds, exit and size change do nothing.
Private ids live in a global store keyed by numeric id. Removal erases present entries; release drops refs and when drained also removes the entry and subsystem pin.

Gen vector startup seeds sequence past the minimum, records enablement, stamps times, inits per-generation lists and seeds per-node sequence. Group startup inits the memory queue and lock when state exists.

Reclaim tracking needs direct reclaim without PF_MEMALLOC and without no-lockdep. Shrinking needs unmapped pagecache or reclaimable slab above thresholds. Estimates clamp dirty subtraction and floor unmapped excess at zero.
Kernel folios count toward memory and kernel tallies, root-owned ordinary folios only as output. Flush applies memory, kernel and legacy adjustments only for nonzero tallies.

Socket charging is gated by a default-off branch with sized charge before counter update on default hierarchy. Swap exhaustion records limit plus failure events; missing cache records only failure and succeeds uncharged.

Folding drains child pending and adds per-CPU deltas to local, hierarchical and optional parent sinks, clearing slots and updating snapshots. One build also merges interrupt-unsafe counters; the other is empty. Fork marks charging lazy and exit clears it safely; reset restores max ceilings, zero protections, disabled group OOM and refreshed sizing.

Limit files show the sentinel as textual maximum and others scaled to bytes. Writes trim whitespace, accept textual maximum, parse to pages and install into min, low, high or ceiling, ceiling via atomic exchange.

locks.text: Lookups racing teardown run under read-side sections with online or counted refs held and no sleepable work. Swap entry updates additionally hold a per-cluster lock only for the update.

Vector startup inits locks and lists, poisoning the unevictable head. Gen online assigns bin and generation then queues under node IRQ lock. Swap offline advances the scan pointer under the shrink lock.

Shrinker alloc, release and reparenting hold the global mutex. Alloc publishes per-node tables with release ordering and unwinds on failure; release frees with matching allocator; reparenting sums child counts into parents.

state_machines.text: Alloc presets max limits, links counters, sets socket and BPF branches and inherits tuning. Online enables kernel memory, allocs shrinker maps and object groups, starts root flushing, onlines gen state and publishes the id with unwind on failure. Offline reparents LRUs, groups and deferred counts, offlines writeback and gen and drains stock; release and free tear down the rest.

Gen reclaim queues address spaces: add resolves owner, fixes sentinel tails and appends; removal fixes links, unlinks and drops the ref; migration re-homes on task-group change, skipping disabled, unregistered or unchanged. Offline rotates all node vectors to aged. Queue mutation holds the per-list lock.

Lowering high or ceiling optionally converges unless nonblocking, stopping on concurrent change, usage below limit, signal or dying group. First pass drains stock, later passes reclaim with swap and bounded retries; ceiling escalates to pressure and OOM on no progress, refreshing writeback sizing on exit.

Peak files mark never-written descriptors with a sentinel. Open installs it; show displays global or larger local watermarks; write snapshots usage, raises lagging peers and registers on first write; release unregisters active descriptors with a fast path for never-written ones. Peak mutation holds the per-group peaks lock.

Node reclaim frees up to a target on one node: establish scheduling, stall, accounting, guards and task state; shrink only when thresholds show material, bounded by target and priority; then restore guards, detach state and report total.

Uncharge batches per-folio releases by group: same-group folios accumulate, group change flushes. Single and multi-folio entries share the accumulator, clearing charge marks and balancing refs once per batch plus once per folio.

structs.text: Per-node records hold stats, object-group list, LRU vector and back pointer, tolerating absent entries. Group state adds counters, writeback with foreign table, gen hooks, shrinker maps, peaks, pressure, socket stamp, kernel id and subsystem linkage.

Aggregation descriptor carries hierarchical and local totals, child pending, optional parent sink, current and prior per-CPU values plus a count. Batch accumulator groups uncharge work by owning group with pointer, node id and memory, kernel and output tallies plus a clearing helper.

Controller bundles lifecycle, flush, attach, fork and exit with default and legacy tables. Memory files cover usage, peak, limits, events, stats, NUMA, OOM and reclaim; swap files cover current, high, max, peak and events. Max id is a low-bits mask; unwritten peak is all-ones; boot tokens opt out socket, kernel and BPF.
